findings.note: AC-024 (requirements.md `## Acceptance Criteria`, AC-024; restated in the REQ-005 body: "`diagnostics[]` by `(id, detail)` tuple") mandates that `diagnostics[]` be stable-sorted by `(id, detail)`. The AC-056 remediation composes the array by concatenation and never sorts it: `_write_evidence` explicitly sorts `capability_evaluations` but leaves `diagnostics` in emission order (per-node warn entries first, summary block entry last). Every entry on this path shares the id `dsl-warn-on-matched-capability`, so the tuple order reduces to `detail` order, and the summary detail ("a predicate evaluation produced an outcome: warn evidence node") is a strict prefix of - hence lexicographically smaller than - every warn detail ("...evidence node at capability_id=..."). The correct sorted array therefore puts the `severity: "block"` summary FIRST; the shipped code emits it LAST. Verified by direct string comparison against the exact literals in `_warn_diagnostic_detail` and the step-9 summary sentence. The breach is not confined to the summary entry: warn entries are appended in Registry-declaration order of `capability_id` (`_evaluate_capabilities` iterates `registry_document["capabilities"]` unsorted), and trigger-scope details render `declaration_index=None` while conditional-facet details render `declaration_index=0`, where `'0' < 'N'` - so a Registry declaring `cap-z` before `cap-a`, or any Capability producing both a trigger-scope and a conditional-scope warn node, yields further out-of-order entries. design.md's `validate-resolver-evidence` contract defines the check-id `array-not-stable-sorted` as firing precisely when "`diagnostics[]` [is] not sorted by `(id, detail)`", so every Resolver Evidence instance this stage writes on the `dsl-warn-on-matched-capability` path is, by this feature's own downstream validator, a non-conformant artifact. This is producer/validator contract breakage introduced by the change the bundle presents as the AC-056 fix.

The assertion introduced to lock the new `diagnostics[]` shape derives its expected ordering by reproducing the implementation's own concatenation (`warn entries + [summary]`) rather than the `(id, detail)` order AC-024 specifies. Consequently the 141/0 GREEN evidence cannot, in principle, detect the AC-024 breach above - the suite would still pass whatever order the production code chose, because the expectation is defined as whatever the production code composes. The RED log (138/3) proves only that a missing per-node warn entry is detected, not that ordering is constrained. The contract's mutation-kill claim is likewise weakened: both mutations it names (a second summary entry; collapsing per-node warn entries into one) are cardinality mutations, and no recorded mutation targets ordering.

AC-056 requires each `severity: "warn"` entry's detail to name that node's `capability_id`/`component_id`/`declaration_index` location. The `declaration_index`-bearing half of that rule is produced only by `_evaluate_capabilities`'s conditional-facet warn-collection loop, and no fixture anywhere in this bundle exercises it: the sole T-004 Registry fixture (`lite-check-source-undefined/capability-registry.json`) declares `"conditional_facets": []`, and all three `dsl-warn-*` expectations carry `conditional_facet_evaluations: []` or omit the key. Every warn entry in the recorded evidence is trigger-scope with `declaration_index=None`. The conditional-facet warn path - and with it AC-056's distinctness guarantee for two warn nodes sharing a `(capability_id, component_id)` pair but differing in `declaration_index` - is production code shipped with zero coverage in the evidence presented. The contract defers the cardinality assertions to T-005's TEST-056, whose suite and contract are not in this bundle, so that deferral is an unverified claim here. Relatedly, REQ-004 states `declaration_index` is named "only for a `conditional_facets[].when` node", but `_warn_diagnostic_detail` renders `declaration_index=None` unconditionally for trigger-scope nodes.

findings.ref: specs/epic-193-a5-capability-resolver/human-copy/plugins/sdd-quality-loop/scripts/resolve-project-context.py :: main(), the three `except` handlers around `_evaluate_capabilities` (registry-validation-failed / dependency-subprocess-failed / dependency-output-malformed)
findings.note: `_evaluate_capabilities` mutates `warn_diagnostics` in place as it walks, but these three block call sites pass only `capability_evaluations` and not `warn_diagnostics`, so any per-node WARN records already collected before the dependency failure are silently discarded - even though the sibling `capability_evaluations` list is deliberately preserved for exactly this partial-abort case. REQ-004 requires `diagnostics` to record "every diagnostic-worthy condition this invocation encountered, not only the first/fatal one". The same REQ-004 paragraph also forbids the id appearing with warn entries and no block summary, so the two rules are in tension and the chosen behaviour is defensible - but the tension is undocumented and no fixture covers a warn-node-then-dependency-failure ordering.

All three recheck dependency failures (canonicalizer failure or malformed output, `resolve-component-paths` failure, `generate-registry-digest` failure) are re-raised as `SnapshotGenerationMismatch`, so the emitted diagnostic line asserts "a pre-publication recheck ... detected drift since this invocation's own snapshot" when the actual cause is a subprocess failure. `canonicalizer-invocation-failed`, `dependency-subprocess-failed` and `dependency-output-malformed` are separate rows of the same sixteen-value enum and are the accurate ids for those causes (AC-014 requires `<detail>` to be a canonical, accurate Resolver-owned sentence). Behaviour stays fail-closed, and the sole `snapshot-generation-mismatch` fixture exercises only the genuine digest-drift path, so this mapping is untested.

findings.ref: reports/implementation/epic-193-a5-capability-resolver/T-004.md `## Second Pass - AC-056 Remediation` Outputs table; verification/T-004/{red,green}-ac056-{sh,ps1}.log
findings.note: The report records identical SHA-256 values for the sh and ps1 members of each pair (`cbf8a287...` for both RED logs, `b751fe96...` for both GREEN logs), and the bundled focused-tests-{sh,ps1}.log pair is byte-identical in size (9623 bytes, same 4327-byte elision). No assertion label in these logs carries a runtime marker, so a PowerShell log is byte-indistinguishable from a copy of the POSIX one. The claimed pwsh green - the evidence backing the `acceptance-tests` contract check - therefore cannot be independently verified from this bundle. Emitting the runtime into the log header would make the twin falsifiable.
